Responsible for leading a team that performs a range of accounting activities to ensure compliance with accounting standards, regulations, and company policies. This role oversees the preparation and analysis of financial reports, maintains strong internal controls, and drives continuous improvement initiatives. The Finance and Accounting Manager develops processes and procedures to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of accounting operations. The position collaborates extensively with cross-functional stakeholders and provides guidance, coaching, and performance management for team members.
Key Responsibilities
Manage day-to-day operations of the accounting function, including general ledger, journal entries, reconciliations, accounts payable, and accounts receivable.
Supervise the preparation of financial statements, reports, and analyses for management and regulatory purposes.
Ensure accounting records are maintained accurately and in compliance with US GAAP and internal policies.
Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual closing activities and ensure timely reporting.
Oversee the development, implementation, and maintenance of accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls.
Identify opportunities to improve accounting processes, systems, and tools, and lead related initiatives.
Serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external auditors and regulatory agencies.
Provide coaching, mentoring, and performance management for accounting staff.
Collaborate with finance and business partners to support operational and strategic objectives.
Contribute to budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning processes as needed.
Core Competencies
Execution
Analyzes and prioritizes the varying aspects of the role, knows and follows the most effective and efficient processes to get things done, and consistently achieves results, even under tough circumstances.
Collaboration
Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives through effective communication that understands the unique needs of different audiences.
Innovation
Creates new and better ways for the organization to be successful; anticipates and adopts innovations in business, operations, and technology applications.
Adaptability
Adapts and pivots in real time to match the shifting demands of different situations, and moves forward productively and optimistically under conditions of change and ambiguity.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Strong knowledge of US GAAP, revenue recognition, and regulatory requirements.
Proficiency with ERP systems and advanced reporting tools.
Ability to lead, motivate, and develop high-performing accounting teams.
Excellent analytical skills to resolve complex accounting issues.
Project management skills to drive improvements and ensure deadlines are met.
Strong business acumen and understanding of financial processes.
Effective communication skills to engage and influence stakeholders across functions.
Ability to balance strategic priorities with operational execution.
Typical Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
CPA or equivalent certification strongly preferred.
8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including prior leadership experience.
Demonstrated success managing accounting operations and implementing process improvements.
We are interested in all qualified candidates who are eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position.
The base pay range for this position is between $130,000.00 to $150,000.00 annually. Base pay will depend on multiple individualized factors, including, but not limited to, internal equity, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  This range represents a good-faith estimate of compensation at the time of posting. Boston Dynamics offers a generous Benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off, and an annual bonus structure.  Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer for employment.
#LI-CG1

About Dexterity
Dexterity is the enterprise Physical AI company building intelligent robots for complex industrial work.
Dexterity's Mech systems combine the Foresight World Model, robotics, and a Physical AI platform to perform demanding logistics workflows - including trailer loading, trailer unloading, and airport baggage handling - at the speed, reliability, and safety levels required for high-volume operations. Dexterity's Foresight World Model powers real-time perception, planning, and execution across physical environments with the interpretability required for industrial deployment. Dexterity is headquartered in Redwood City, California.
Dexterity is backed by world-class investors such as Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Obvious Ventures. We are a diverse and multidisciplinary team with a culture built on passion, trust, and dedication.
  
Job Summary
Dexterity is seeking a detail-oriented Staff Accountant to join our Finance team. This role will support day-to-day accounting operations with primary responsibility for accounts payable, payroll administration, general ledger reconciliations, and month-end close activities.
The ideal candidate is hands-on, highly organized, and comfortable working across multiple accounting processes in a fast-paced environment. You'll partner closely with Finance, People, and other cross-functional teams to ensure accurate and timely financial and payroll processing.This role requires strong analytical skills, a solid understanding of GAAP principles, and the ability to collaborate across departments to streamline financial operations.
This is a fully onsite position and is based in Redwood City, CA.
Key Responsibilities
Month-End Close
Execute month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities according to the corporate schedule.
Prepare and record journal entries with complete supporting documentation.
Reconcile balance sheet accounts monthly, including cash, prepaid expenses, accruals, and fixed assets.
Identify, investigate, and resolve accounting variances and discrepancies promptly.
Assist in preparing monthly financial statements, schedules, and management reports.
Accounts Payable and Vendor Management
Review, code, and process all incoming vendor invoices with high accuracy.
Match invoices to purchase orders and receiving documents using standard 3-way matching rules.
Manage the weekly payment run schedule.
Research and resolve invoice discrepancies or billing issues with vendors and internal teams.
Maintain clean vendor files and manage the annual 1099 tax reporting process.
Payroll Administration
Process accurate and timely biweekly payroll using ADP.
Review and validate timesheets, hourly wages, overtime, deductions, and other payroll inputs.
Process payroll changes related to new hires, terminations, compensation, benefits, and other employee changes.
Ensure accurate processing of payroll taxes, garnishments, deductions, and other required adjustments.
Partner closely with People Operations to ensure employee and payroll data are accurate and properly maintained.
Research and resolve payroll discrepancies and employee payroll inquiries.
Qualifications and Skills
Experience: 2+ years of accounting experience, including hands-on experience with accounts payable, general ledger accounting, and month-end close. Payroll experience is strongly preferred.
Software: Experience with a large ERP system (Netsuite or similar) and ADP Workforce Now highly preferred.. 
Tools: Strong Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookup functions, and working with large data sets.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field preferred.
Competencies: 
Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Ability to manage competing priorities and meet recurring deadlines.
Strong problem-solving and reconciliation skills.
Ability to handle confidential payroll and employee information with discretion.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.
Comfortable working independently while collaborating across Finance, People, and other teams.


Compensation
Base pay is one component of Dexterity's Total Rewards package, which may also include equity, comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits, and other compensation elements depending on eligibility.
The annual base salary range for this position is $85,000 - $110,000 USD. Actual compensation will be determined based on relevant experience, skills, scope, qualifications, market factors, and internal equity.
 
Equal Opportunity Employer
Dexterity is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all employees and applicants are treated with fairness and respect.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, ancestry, national origin, citizenship status, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), reproductive health decision-making, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, medical condition, genetic information, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
Dexterity is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and to applicants who require accommodations during the hiring process, consistent with applicable law. If you require an accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know.

We are looking for a highly analytical and execution-oriented operator to work closely with the CFO on the company’s most important strategic initiatives. This role sits at the intersection of finance, strategy, operations, and external partnerships, supporting critical decisions as we scale across customers, products, and markets.
The ideal candidate combines strong financial and strategic thinking with the ability to operate in fast-moving, technically complex environments. You will work cross-functionally across leadership, engineering, go-to-market, and external stakeholders to drive execution on high-impact initiatives across AI, robotics, and real-world infrastructure deployments.
What You Will Do
Partner directly with the CFO and leadership team on high-priority strategic, operational, and commercial initiatives
Support strategic partnerships, financing activities, market expansion opportunities, and other high-impact corporate initiatives
Conduct market, competitive, operational, and financial analysis across robotics, AI, industrial, manufacturing, and infrastructure sectors
Evaluate new business opportunities, strategic relationships, and adjacent market opportunities
Own projects end-to-end from analysis through execution across internal and external stakeholders
Lead cross-functional initiatives spanning finance, operations, engineering, and go-to-market teams
Analyze company performance and key business drivers to support strategic decision-making
Build and improve internal processes to increase efficiency and scalability across the organization
Develop materials and recommendations for executive leadership, investors, customers, and strategic partners
Work closely with senior leadership on company-critical decisions and initiatives
Required Qualifications
4–8 years of experience across investment banking, private equity, consulting, strategic finance, corporate strategy, or high-growth technology companies
Intellectual curiosity around AI, robotics, and real-world deployment challenges
Strong analytical, problem-solving and financial modeling skills
Comfortable operating in technically complex environments and collaborating closely with engineering, product, and operational teams
Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative or technical field such as Engineering, Economics, Finance, Mathematics, Physics, or Computer Science
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience at a high-growth startup or operating company
Experience within industrials, infrastructure, aerospace & defense, enterprise technology, robotics, AI, manufacturing, energy, construction, logistics, or related sectors
Exposure to strategic partnerships, financings, investor relations, corporate development, or other transaction-oriented initiatives
Location
Irvine / Orange County preferred


Why Join Field AI?
We are solving one of the world’s most complex challenges: deploying robots in unstructured, previously unknown environments. Our Field Foundational Models™ set a new standard in perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, ensuring our approach is explainable and safe for deployment.
 
You will have the opportunity to work with a world-class team that thrives on creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. With a decade-long track record of deploying solutions in the field, winning DARPA challenge segments, and bringing expertise from organizations like DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise Self-Driving, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX, we are set to achieve our ambitious goals.
 
Be Part of the Next Robotics Revolution
To tackle such ambitious challenges, we need a team as unique as our vision — innovators who go beyond conventional methods and are eager to tackle tough, uncharted questions. We’re seeking individuals who challenge the status quo, dive into uncharted territory, and bring interdisciplinary expertise. Our team requires not only top AI talent but also exceptional software developers, engineers, product designers, field deployment experts, and communicators.
 
We are headquartered in always-sunny Irvine, Southern California and have US based and global teammates. 
 
Join us, shape the future, and be part of a fun, close-knit team on an exciting journey!
 
 
 
We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

Como
Facilities Coordinator (Coordenador(a) de Facilities)
, você é o dono da operação predial da nossa unidade de São Paulo, de ponta a ponta: serviços do prédio, segurança terceirizada e gestão de prestadores. Você será uma das primeiras contratações no Brasil, montando as rotinas e mantendo a unidade segura, funcional e pronta para uma operação em rápido crescimento.
Esta é uma posição em tempo integral e presencial, na nossa unidade de São Paulo.
Responsabilidades
Conduzir a operação predial: manutenção, limpeza, utilidades e serviços de workplace para uma única unidade.
Gerenciar os fornecedores terceirizados de segurança (vigilância e CFTV) como ponto de contato responsável.
Gerenciar prestadores e fornecedores de serviços: apoio à seleção, agendamento, acesso à unidade, qualidade e acompanhamento.
Ser o dono dos contratos de fornecedores, SLAs (acordos de nível de serviço) e chamados; definir rotinas de escalação e conduzir os problemas até a resolução.
Liderar projetos de adequação e melhoria da unidade em parceria com a liderança local.
Estabelecer e manter as rotinas e a documentação de segurança do trabalho junto aos prestadores externos.
Construir o playbook (manual de processos) de facilities, incluindo processos, fornecedores e orçamentos, conforme a unidade escala.

4-8 anos em facilities, workplace ou gestão predial, com histórico comprovado de responsabilidade por uma unidade ou frente.
Experiência gerenciando fornecedores e prestadores terceirizados com autonomia.
Perfil organizado e mão na massa, confortável em ser o único dono de tudo que envolve o prédio.
Inglês em nível profissional (coordenação escrita e falada com times nos EUA).
Diferenciais
Experiência em unidades industriais, galpões ou ambientes mistos de escritório e operação.
Experiência abrindo ou montando uma nova unidade.
Familiaridade com as Normas Regulamentadoras (NRs) de segurança do trabalho.
Remuneração
Salário base:
R$ 7.000 a R$ 11.000 por mês
Benefícios:
vale-transporte, vale-refeição e plano de saúde

A Figure é uma empresa de robótica e IA que desenvolve robôs humanoides autônomos de uso geral. O objetivo da empresa é lançar robôs humanoides com inteligência de nível humano. Seus robôs são projetados para executar uma grande variedade de tarefas nos mercados residencial e comercial. A Figure tem sede em San Jose, Califórnia, e está estabelecendo sua primeira unidade de operações de dados no Brasil.
Como
Finance Operations Manager (Gerente de Operações Financeiras)
, você é o principal parceiro financeiro do time de operações no Brasil. Este papel conecta finanças e execução em campo: traduz a atividade operacional em informação financeira, promove disciplina de custos e garante que o negócio tenha os dados necessários para tomar decisões rápidas e bem fundamentadas à medida que a operação no Brasil escala. Você será uma das primeiras contratações no Brasil, construindo as fundações de finanças da unidade.
Esta é uma posição em tempo integral e presencial, na nossa unidade de São Paulo.
Responsabilidades
Atuar como parceiro financeiro integrado aos times de Operações, People e Jurídico no Brasil.
Apoiar a estruturação da entidade brasileira, incluindo registros regulatórios, gestão de contas bancárias, modelagem de custos e planejamento de cenários.
Garantir que os processos financeiros cumpram os requisitos regulatórios brasileiros (e.g., Receita Federal, eSocial, INSS, FGTS).
Ser o dono do orçamento de operações no Brasil, das previsões mensais e das estimativas contínuas (rolling forecasts).
Construir e manter modelos financeiros para apoiar o planejamento de headcount, custos de fornecedores e despesas de instalações.
Traduzir decisões operacionais (ritmo de contratação, seleção de fornecedores, adequação de instalações) em implicações financeiras.
Rastrear e reportar todos os custos operacionais no Brasil: folha de pagamento, benefícios, instalações, logística e serviços de terceiros.
Identificar oportunidades de economia e exercer governança sobre as aprovações de gastos.
Trabalhar com fornecedores (BPO de folha de pagamento, agências de staffing, assessoria jurídica) em benchmarking de tarifas e condições contratuais.
Manter controles internos sobre folha de pagamento, contas a pagar e relatórios de despesas.
Apoiar auditorias externas e obrigações acessórias e estatutárias à medida que a entidade amadurece.
Produzir relatórios financeiros claros e concisos para a liderança no Brasil e para os stakeholders na matriz (HQ) nos EUA.
Construir dashboards e ferramentas de acompanhamento que ofereçam visibilidade em tempo real sobre os gastos operacionais.
Apresentar análises e recomendações à alta liderança em português e inglês.
Requisitos
Graduação em Finanças, Contabilidade, Economia ou área relacionada; registro CRC ativo é um diferencial.
5+ anos de experiência em finanças de operações ou funções de controladoria.
Experiência apoiando expansão de negócios, constituição de entidade ou estruturação de operação local será altamente valorizada.
Sólidas habilidades de modelagem financeira (Excel/Google Sheets); familiaridade com sistemas ERP (NetSuite, SAP, etc.).
Conforto em operar em um ambiente de ritmo acelerado e alta ambiguidade, com infraestrutura limitada.
Inglês em nível profissional (relatórios e coordenação frequente com times nos EUA), além de português fluente.
Diferenciais
Experiência prévia com legislação trabalhista brasileira (CLT), compliance de folha de pagamento ou constituição de entidades.
Exposição a operações em robótica, manufatura ou setor de tecnologia.
Experiência com BPOs de folha de pagamento ou provedores de EOR.
Experiência em startup, abertura de unidade ou crescimento acelerado de time.
Remuneração
Salário base:
R$ 15.000 a R$ 25.000 por mês, conforme senioridade e experiência
Benefícios:
vale-transporte, vale-refeição e plano de saúde

Employee Lifecycle & Experience
Own the employee lifecycle end-to-end (onboarding, job changes, offboarding, records, verifications), ensuring every step is seamless, compliant, and audit ready.
Continuously audit and elevate the employee experience, gathering feedback to remove operational friction and build a high empathy, high efficiency workplace.
Serve as a trusted point of contact for employee HR inquiries, resolving tickets within SLAs and handling complex escalations with judgment and discretion.
Manage statutory leaves end-to-end and lead interactive medical accommodation processes, coordinating state disability integration, communications, and return-to-work logistics.
Serve as the compliance escalation point for garnishments, complex leave cases, and sensitive offboarding events.
Payroll, Benefits & Hourly Workforce
Run accurate, end-to-end payroll for exempt and non-exempt teams, including final pay calculations, severance, and leave-related adjustments.
Maintain strict timekeeping hygiene across hourly populations, tracking daily punch accuracy, shift differentials, and meal/rest break compliance.
Partner with our benefits broker to manage health, 401(k), and wellness programs; lead annual Open Enrollment and evaluate benefit competitiveness.
Audit and reconcile monthly carrier billings, benefit feeds, and agency staffing invoices to eliminate financial discrepancies.

Serve as primary system administrator for our People tech stack (HRIS, timekeeping, ticketing), managing configurations, permissions, workflows, and integrations.
Partner with the broader People team on compensation and job architecture (levels, job families, pay bands), keeping system data clean and current.
Partner with People Partner to build and maintain a centralized People Ops knowledge repository (SOPs, handbooks, compliance calendars) to maximize self-service support.

Lead cross-functional People projects as we scale, from org design updates to vendor evaluations and policy rollouts.
